Shankar Yadav @ Shanker Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on
16 June, 2023
Author: Navneet Kumar

Bench: Navneet Kumar
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
 Cr. Appeal (S.J.) No. 40 of 2023
 Shankar Yadav @ Shanker Yadav --- --- Appellant
 Versus
 1.The State of Jharkhand
 2.Kali Devi --- --- Respondent
 .......
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Navneet Kumar For the Petitioner : Mr. Rajesh Kumar,
Advocate For the State : Mr. Rakesh Ranjan, A.P.P. 04/16.06.2023

entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant and the learned A.P.P. appearing on behalf of the State.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that defects as pointed out by the Office has been removed by filing supplementary affidavit.
Further, it has been submitted that one interlocutory application being I.A. No. 3601 of 2023 has been filed for condonation of delay of 70 days in filing the instant criminal appeal.

It is submitted on behalf of the appellant that the impugned order rejecting the anticipatory bail petition of the petitioner in A.B.P. No. 1103 of 2022 was passed by the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI, Hazaribag on 06.08.2022 however he came to know about this fact from his counsel on 23.12.2022, where after he took steps for filing of this appeal,
which has occasioned some delay and there is no willful default and latches on the part of the appellant and if the delay is not condoned, he will suffer irreparably.
3. Having taken into consideration the aforesaid submission and the reasons assigned in the instant I.A., delay is condoned.
I.A. No. 3601 of 2023 is disposed of 4.

Learned A.P.P. appearing on behalf of the State submitted that one counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the State submitting inter alia that notice has been served upon the informant as far back on 04.02.2023 but the respondent no.2 did not choose to appear in this appeal.

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submitted that appellant has been falsely implicated in this case by the respondent no.2 Kali Devi @ Kanu Devi in view of the fact that on earlier occasion the respondent no.2 had instituted a case being Jainagar P.S. Case No. 232 of 2018 registered under Section 341/323/498A of the IPC on 16.09.2018 and the copy of the F.I.R. is annexed with the instant appeal at Annexure-2, which is available on record.
Subsequently, after completion of investigation in the aforesaid F.I.R the final form was submitted by the Investigating Officer exonerating the appellant from the charges levelled against him.

It is further submitted that Shankar Yadav @ Shanker Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131714668/
1

entities.text: Shankar Yadav @ Shanker Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the version of respondent no. 2 in the aforesaid fact is not trustworthy and in the present case she has made the allegation of rape, while the earlier case instituted by her was with regard to matrimonial dispute of torture and cruelty alleged to have been caused by the appellant and therefore, the entire allegations are false and fabricated.
Therefore, appellant deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

6. On the other hand learned A.P.P. appearing on behalf of the State has opposed the contention raised on behalf of the appellant and submitted that the present case has been instituted against the appellant by the informant for attempt to rape and he also humiliated the informant by making offending remarks about her lower caste and since this is an anticipatory bail application, therefore,
he does not deserve to be enlarge on bail.
7 . It is found that despite proper notice served upon respondent no.2- informant, she did not choose to appear.

Further it is found that on earlier occasion the respondent no.2 had instituted a case against the appellant for torture and cruelty under Section 498A IPC against the appellant being Jainagar P.S. Case No. 232 of 2018 for the offence registered under Section 341,323,498A/34 IPC in which it is stated that final form was submitted absolving the appellant from the charges levelled against him.

Further from the contents of the F.I.R it has been pointed out that there had been a relationship between both of them and there is no specific allegation of any kind of humiliation or harassing the informant by hurling abusive language by taking name of her caste as such no offence under the SC/ST is made out.
8.

Hence in the light of the rulings of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hitesh Verma Vrs.
State of Jharkhand & another reported in (2020) 10 SCC 710, the appellant deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

State of Jharkhand & another reported in (2020) 10 SCC 710
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Accordingly, the appellant, named above, is directed to surrender within a period of 2 weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order, in the court below and the learned Court below is directed to enlarge the appellant in the event of his arrest or/ surrender on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of Learned Additional Sessions Judge VI, Hazaribag in connection with Barhi P.S. Case No. 07 of 2022, subject to the condition as set out under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C. and further condition that appellant will cooperate in the criminal proceeding in the court below and appear before the Investigating Officer / Court below as and when required by them, failing which, the learned court below shall take appropriate steps for cancellation of bail of this appellant.
10.
Instant criminal appeal is allowed.

The impugned order dated 06.08.2022 passed in A.B.P. No.
1103 of 2022 by the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI, Hazaribag is set aside.

(Navneet Kumar, J.) A.Mohanty Shankar Yadav @ Shanker Yadav vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131714668/
